items.title: John Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 18, 2023 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: And Don Sebesky wrote the arrangement for the cello and Ken Peplowski and Harry Allen and Dominick.

ctx.x: It is indeed. It’s a beautiful song and I just was listening to it and I loved it when the accordion came in and I got this sense of your family history and Bucky talking about the accordion and all that. And so I just wanted to say nice going, and Jessica, I don’t know how this line came up to be but there’s the line that it sort of waits to get to, and then “What DaVinci would do with your eyes.”

That’s a great line. It’s a great song. And what happened was it’s based on well Dominick Cortese plays the accordion and he’s a family friend. And he’s the accordion player on, there’s a song called “Where’s the Orchestra” that ends the “Allentown” record, Billy Joel’s record. And it’s similar to that kind of thing. And I always loved that sound. And Don Sebesky wrote the arrangement for the cello and Ken Peplowski and Harry Allen and Dominick. Because Sebesky’s an old — was an old accordion player. And I sort…
Well they do, at least I do.
